claim: Every AI-written email uses a bottle of water.
scope: Any email written with any AI chatbot, as the headline implies.
occurrence: Paraphrase of The Washington Post headline “A bottle of water per email: the hidden environmental costs of using AI chatbots” (Pranshu Verma and Shelly Tan, September 18, 2024), which reported a university researchers’ estimate that one 100-word email written with GPT-4 used 519 milliliters of water. Wording of the estimate confirmed through TechRepublic’s September 20, 2024 summary; the Post page itself returned an access error at cutoff.

P1.reason: States as a measured fact what is a modelled estimate. Per-request water figures combine an assumed energy use per request with location-specific water-intensity factors, including water used to generate the electricity.

P2.reason: Extends an estimate for one 100-word email from one model to every AI email, of any length, from any model and data center. Water use varies widely with location, cooling and power source.

W1.reason: A bottle (about half a liter) matches the size of the reported estimate; the comparison adds no further exaggeration.

W2.reason: No human-like agency is attributed to AI.

review_status: AI research draft; not independently reviewed
note: Headline claim added October 6, 2026 at Leyla’s request for spicier headlines. Scored with the same claims-us-1.0 rubric; evidence comes from the topic research brief.
